reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Same-cell electrophysiology and calcium imaging with spike-pattern calibration and optical-reference/motion comparisons.

checks.reason: Defines independently recorded spikes as the positive reference, matched-count/timing or absent-spike comparisons as the biological negative/null, and motion/structural reference checks as procedural controls. These role-defined comparisons suffice for the chosen B-minus-A validation; a literal web search is not required.

No explicit pre-execution consultation of indicator/paired-recording Methods or validated protocols to select detailed conditions and verify transfer. A generic published calibration mention is insufficient.

Proposes spike/fluorescence calibration but does not specify a measurement-error/noise or recovery acceptance criterion and the action if calibration fails; a fitted curve or plateau inspection alone is incomplete.

No fully defined endpoint with baseline/background calculation, units/denominator and weak/near-zero/saturated/missing-signal handling. Naming delta-F/F and spike counts is not the complete measurement rule.

checks.quote: exclude trials whose fluorescence tracks movement
checks.reason: Outcome-correlated motion exclusion may remove real movement-linked neural responses; no independent artifact threshold or alternative ambiguity rule protects this decision.

Operational simultaneous electrical spike recording and imaging of the same cell provides an independent measurement; comparisons of count/timing and fluorescence, with acknowledged optical/calcium ambiguities, meet essay-scale validation. Extra optional reporters are not treated as independent ground truth.

checks.quote: prevent individual spikes from being resolved
checks.reason: Slow kinetics limit resolution but do not categorically prevent resolving isolated spikes at adequate SNR and sampling.

Connects kinetics, calibration, motion and saturation to an independent validation proposal; the principal spike-count inference is limited. No additional distinct content, evidence-status or format defect beyond the recorded deductions.
